chapter: Recording with King Oliver and Clarence Williams
title: Why the Oliver dates meant little beside Charlie Johnson's band
summary: Waters says he answered European questions about Oliver sarcastically because Charlie Johnson's band, with Harrison, Carter, Dickie Wells and Billy Taylor, was more advanced, and the records paid only extra money.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: But you're saying you have a record of "Snag It" with you and King Oliver -
Yeah, I bought a record of, with "Snag It", yeah -
That's what it says on the sleeve.

I remember the song. You see, I'll tell you about this King Oliver, 'cause I'd get in the same arguments in Europe, you know. Rather lot of people in Europe says I didn't record with - no, no, they didn't say I didn't because they couldn't say that. They said "Did you really record with King Oliver?" So I used to be drinkin', you know, I used to be drinkin' and I heard that so much - "Did you record with King-", you know. At least it was such a great band, and I'm working with a great band with Charlie Johnson, such guys as Jimmy Harrison, all that kind of stuff - Sidney de Paris, Edgar Sampson, Benny Carter, Billy Taylor, a greater bass horn player than Sy Oliver, Sy -

Billy Taylor was one of the greatest of the bass players I ever heard, bass horn, you know. I'm working in a great band, that was just some extry money. So when those guys in Europe says "Did you really work with King Oliver?" I could, I would get sarcastic and told 'em that "No", like I got tired of answering the question, you know what I mean? 'Cause he wasn't that big to me, you know, see what I mean - he was big to the public, because - "King Oliver, that's great!" I worked with a better band, see what I mean? See, so naturally, I was [ ], [ ] egotistical a little bit with that deal, because I was working on big time. We had more advanced musicians in it, you know what mean? Not prestigious, but advanced musically - Benny Carter and Billy Taylor and all those cats like that, Dickie Wells and Sidney de Paris, see what I mean?

It was a different thing there altogether, I'm workin', just makin' some money. That's why I didn't hear the record, because it - and when I recorded in that period, the records didn't come out until a month. And I don't know, I don't even, I didn't hear the records, some of them only heard when guys in Europe says "Hey, Benny, I bought this record at the Gare Lafayette and I saw that, saw your name on it". You see what I mean?
